title: CacheCraft: Enhancing GPU Performance under Memory Protection through Reconstructed Caching
problem: In-band ECC protection in GPUs with GDDR memory requires sequential access of data and redundancy, reducing data throughput and causing significant performance penalties (up to 96.9% increase in memory accesses) for bandwidth-intensive applications.
motivation: GPU memory reliability via ECC is essential for error protection, but the access overhead substantially degrades performance of bandwidth-intensive workloads.
method: CacheCraft rearranges each 128-byte memory chunk into four 30-byte sections and one 8-byte section (instead of the standard four equal 32-byte sections), creating 2 bytes per section to store ECC (error-correcting code that catches and fixes memory bit errors) alongside the actual data. By packing the ECC with the data in the same memory chunk, a GPU retrieves both the information and its protection bits in one memory request—avoiding the sequential back-and-forth that traditional systems require, where they fetch data first and then fetch the error-protection information separately.
key_novelty: Integrate error-correcting code into cache line sections so that data and its error protection travel together in a single memory request, instead of requiring separate sequential accesses.
contributions: Novel cache line architecture that embeds ECC redundancy within existing memory chunks without requiring additional memory access
Single-access in-band ECC mechanism reducing memory access overhead from 41.9% to 21.9% (47.8% average reduction, up to 89.4%)
Performance improvements up to 23.5% for memory-intensive applications while maintaining full ECC protection

metrics.other: reduces memory access overhead from 41.9% to 21.9% (peak reduction from 96.9% to 28.2%); 47.8% average reduction in extra bandwidth requirement
